resources.string: Examine the evidence, test alibis, and find the culprit.
Every case is closed. Replay any of them from the collection.
Solve it to unlock one more clue.
All marks in the matrix, the special evidence and the hint counter of this case will be cleared.
Tap a cell: ✕ — ruled out, ✓ — confirmed, a third tap clears it.
Swipe the matrix sideways to see every column.
Locked clue. Solve the special evidence to read it.
Marks that contradict the evidence: %1$d. They are highlighted.
No mistakes so far. Put a ✓ for every suspect in each category to finish.
The matrix is correct. Now use the key fact to name the culprit.
Being somewhere is not the same as being guilty. Read the key fact again and match it with the matrix.
Some marks contradict the evidence. They are highlighted in the matrix — fix them first.
Nothing more follows from the open clues. Solve the special evidence to unlock the last one.
Everything that can be deduced is already in the matrix. Tap “Check”.
Clue %1$d together with the marks you already have gives: %2$s.
Only one option is left for “%1$s” in “%2$s”: %3$s.
%1$s and %2$s belong together, so what is known about one holds for the other: %3$s.
None of the remaining options for “%1$s” in “%2$s” can go with “%3$s”, so: %4$s.
Assume the opposite and the clues run into a contradiction. Therefore: %1$s.
Tap the events in the order they happened. Tap a numbered one to undo.
That does not fit the evidence. Look again.
Presence alone proves nothing — guilt follows from this fact.
Key fact: the crime is tied to “%1$s”. The matrix links it to %2$s — that is the culprit.
Erases solved cases, stars and all marks. Settings are kept.
Every case will return to “not started”. This cannot be undone.
Deductive: Case Files 1.0 · 120 offline cases · no ads, no network
Take a two-minute tour: on one tiny case we will show how to read the clues, fill in the matrix and name the culprit. You can always open it later from the home screen.
Every case has several suspects. Each of them was in exactly one place and had exactly one thing, and no place or thing is shared. The matrix helps you work out who goes with what.
A cell where two names cross asks: “do these two belong together?” ✕ means no, ✓ means yes. One tap puts ✕, a second tap puts ✓, a third clears the cell. Now we go through the clues one by one.
Tap the highlighted cell once to put ✕.
Tap the highlighted cell twice to put ✓. The rest of its row and column is crossed out automatically.

The matrix is complete. In real cases “Hint” explains the next logical step and “Check” highlights mistakes. Some cases also have a piece of special evidence — a cipher, an alibi, a picture — that unlocks one more clue.
The matrix only shows who was where. Guilt follows from the key fact — match it with the matrix and name the culprit.
Well done — that is all there is to it. Harder cases add more suspects, a fourth category and trickier clues, but the reasoning stays the same.
